title: preferences.yml
description: Operator working preferences — the personal layer of an installation. Consumed by the operator's AI agents (via the templates/adopter kit and AGENT_SETUP step 6), never by the bot itself. Lives ONLY in the operator's private governance repo, like every other config/ file. The public framework ships the schema and blank examples; each operator's values stay their own.

language.description: What language your agents speak to you in.

primary.description: Language your agents use when talking to you (IETF-style code).

reports.description: Language for written deliverables (reports, docs). 'primary' = same as primary; 'bilingual' = primary + English side by side.

communication.description: How your agents should report and ask.

report_style.description: 'conclusion-first' = verdict in the first sentence, details after. 'detailed' = full narrative acceptable.

decision_format.description: 'options-menu' = decisions reach you as 2-4 labeled options with pros/cons (good for non-developers). 'direct-question' = plain questions are fine.

batch_questions.description: true = collect questions and ask them together instead of one-at-a-time interruptions.

autonomy.description: How much your agents decide without you. This does NOT change what the bot enforces (Quadrant D always waits for you); it tunes how your agents behave below that line.

profile.description: 'cautious' = agents confirm before anything outward-facing or hard to undo, even when the bot would allow it. 'standard' = agents follow the four-quadrant model as-is. 'delegating' = agents proceed on everything the bot allows and report after.

quiet_hours.description: Daily window when agents must not ping you (24h clock, operator's timezone). Decision Inbox issues still open; notifications wait.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name used to interpret quiet_hours.

taste_ledger.description: Append-only ledger of your declared working preferences — the things you found yourself repeating to agents. Each entry is dated and quotable. Agents read this at session start and follow it; when you state a new preference, your agent should append it here IMMEDIATELY (one statement is enough — do not wait for a repeat).

rule.description: The preference as an actionable one-liner, e.g. 'Never place deliverables in my Downloads folder' or 'Long documents: base font around 14.5px'.

quote.description: Optional: your original words, so future agents understand the intent, not just the rule.

vocabulary.description: Your shorthand: project nicknames, acronyms, internal terms — so agents understand requests the way a colleague would.
